title: A Game of Polo with a Headless Goat
author: Emma Levine
blurb: A chaotic and funny account of a donkey race in Karachi. Vivid description captures the thrilling anarchy of the event.
source: Levine writes about a donkey race in Karachi, Pakistan
heading: From A Game of Polo with a Headless Goat - Emma Levine
context: Levine travelled throughout Asia researching and filming unusual sports. In this passage she writes about a donkey race in Karachi, Pakistan.

paragraphs.html: We drove off to find the best viewing spot, which turned out to be the crest of the hill so we could see the approaching race. I asked the lads if we could join in the 'Wacky Races' and follow the donkeys, and they loved the idea. 'We'll open the car boot, you climb inside and point your camera towards the race. As the donkeys overtake us, we'll join the cars.' 'But will you try and get to the front?' 'Oh yes, that's no problem.'

The two lads who had never been interested in this Karachi sport were suddenly fired up with enthusiasm. We waited for eternity on the brow of the hill, me perched in the boot with a zoom lens pointing out. Nearly one hour later I was beginning to feel rather silly when the only action was a villager on a wobbly bicycle, who nearly fell off as he cycled past and gazed around at us.

Several vehicles went past, and some donkey-carts carrying spectators. 'Are they coming?' we called out to them. 'Coming, coming,' came the reply. I was beginning to lose faith in its happening, but the lads remained confident.

Just as I was assuming that the race had been cancelled, we spotted two approaching donkey-carts in front of a cloud of fumes and dust created by some fifty vehicles roaring up in their wake. As they drew nearer, Yaqoob revved up the engine and began to inch the car out of the lay-by. The two donkeys were almost dwarfed by their entourage; but there was no denying their speed — the Kibla donkey is said to achieve speeds of up to 40 kph, and this looked close. The two were neck-and-neck, their jockeys perched on top of the tiny carts using their whips energetically, although not cruelly.

The noise of the approaching vehicles grew; horns tooting, bells ringing, and the special rattles used just for this purpose (like maracas, a metal container filled with dried beans). Men standing on top of their cars and vans, hanging out of taxis and perched on lorries, all cheered and shouted, while the vehicles jostled to get to the front of the convoy.

Yaqoob chose exactly the right moment to edge out of the road and swerve in front of the nearest car, finding the perfect place to see the two donkeys and at the front of the vehicles. This was Formula One without rules, or a city-centre rush hour gone anarchic; a complete flouting of every type of traffic rule and common sense.

Our young driver relished this unusual test of driving skills. It was survival of the fittest, and depended upon the ability to cut in front of a vehicle with a sharp flick of the steering wheel (no lane discipline here); quick reflexes to spot a gap in the traffic for a couple of seconds; nerves of steel, and an effective horn. There were two races — the motorized spectators at the back; in front, the two donkeys, still running close and amazingly not put off by the uproar just behind them. Ahead of the donkeys, oncoming traffic — for it was a main road — had to dive into the ditch and wait there until we had passed. Yaqoob loved it. We stayed near to the front, his hand permanently on the horn and his language growing more colourful with every vehicle that tried to cut in front. ...

The road straightened and levelled, and everyone picked up speed as we neared the end of the race. But just as they were reaching the finishing line, the hospital gate, there was a near pile-up as the leading donkey swerved, lost his footing and he and the cart tumbled over. The race was over.

And then the trouble began. I assumed the winner was the one who completed the race but it was not seen that way by everyone. Apart from the two jockeys and 'officials' (who, it turned out, were actually monitoring the race) there were over a hundred punters who had all staked money on the race, and therefore had strong opinions. Some were claiming that the donkey had fallen because the other one had been ridden too close to him. Voices were raised, fists were out and tempers rising. Everyone gathered around one jockey and official, while the bookmakers were trying to insist that the race should be re-run.

Yaqoob and Iqbal were nervous of hanging around a volatile situation. They agreed to find out for me what was happening, ordering me to stay inside the car as they were swallowed up by the crowd. They emerged some time later. 'It's still not resolved,' said Iqbal, 'but it's starting to get nasty. I think we should leave.' As we drove away, Yaqoob reflected on his driving skills. 'I really enjoyed that,' he said as we drove off at a more sedate pace. 'But I don't even have my licence yet because I'm underage!'

They both found this hilarious, but I was glad he hadn't told me before; an inexperienced, underage driver causing a massive pile-up in the middle of the high-stakes donkey race could have caused problems.

wacky-races.what: References 1960s cartoon about chaotic car races.
wacky-races.effect: Makes foreign event familiar and comedic for Western readers.

try-front.quote: But will you try and get to the front?
try-front.what: Shows Levine's enthusiasm to fully participate.
try-front.effect: Establishes her as adventurous, not just passive observer.

no-problem.what: Drivers' nonchalant attitude to dangerous driving.
no-problem.effect: Foreshadows the chaos to come. Cultural difference in risk.

never-interested.effect: Makes their later enthusiasm more dramatic.

suddenly-fired.what: Shows how Levine's enthusiasm infects the drivers.
suddenly-fired.effect: Universal appeal of competition transcends cultural boundaries.

eternity.what: Exaggerates the waiting time for comic effect.

perched-boot.quote: perched in the boot with a zoom lens pointing out
perched-boot.what: Creates ridiculous image of professional filmmaker in car boot.
perched-boot.effect: Self-deprecating humour about lengths she'll go for a story.

rather-silly.what: Understated British response to absurd situation.
rather-silly.effect: Maintains dignity through humour. Cultural voice.

wobbly-bicycle.what: Only action is one wobbly cyclist - comic disappointment.
wobbly-bicycle.effect: Heightens anticipation by showing how quiet it is before the storm.

coming-coming.what: Repetition suggests Pakistani time - things happen when they happen.
coming-coming.effect: Shows cultural difference in timekeeping and precision.

lose-faith.effect: Creates tension - will it actually happen?

remained-confident.what: Locals understand the rhythms, outsider doesn't.
remained-confident.effect: Shows cultural insider vs outsider perspective.

cloud-fumes.what: Visual and implied smell/taste of pollution.
cloud-fumes.effect: Makes the convoy's arrival apocalyptic and overwhelming.

roaring-wake.what: 'Wake' usually for ships - makes land vehicles seem naval.
roaring-wake.effect: Emphasises the wave-like force of the following vehicles.

revved-up.what: Sound of engine preparing for action.
revved-up.effect: Builds tension - the moment before joining chaos.

inch-car.what: Contrasts with later wild driving - last moment of control.
inch-car.effect: Shows skill needed even to join the race.

almost-dwarfed.what: Tiny donkeys overshadowed by massive convoy.
almost-dwarfed.effect: Makes the donkeys seem heroic, the convoy absurd.

40-kph.what: Specific speed gives credibility to the account.
40-kph.effect: Surprises readers - donkeys faster than expected.

neck-and-neck.what: Classic racing terminology for close competition.
neck-and-neck.effect: Elevates donkey race to proper sporting event.

energetically-not-cruelly.what: Anticipates Western concerns about animal welfare.
energetically-not-cruelly.effect: Shows cultural sensitivity - not all foreign practices are cruel.

horns-bells.what: List of sounds creates auditory chaos.

like-maracas.quote: like maracas, a metal container filled with dried beans
like-maracas.what: Explains foreign object through familiar comparison.
like-maracas.effect: Makes exotic accessible while maintaining humour.

standing-hanging.quote: standing on top of their cars and vans, hanging out of taxis and perched on lorries
standing-hanging.what: Catalogue of dangerous positions people adopt.
standing-hanging.effect: Shows complete abandonment of safety for spectacle.

jostled.what: Vehicles competing physically like people in crowd.
jostled.effect: Personifies vehicles - they're as competitive as drivers.

exactly-right.effect: Brief moment of control before chaos.

formula-one.what: F1 is all about rules - this removes them.
formula-one.effect: Makes chaos comprehensible through familiar reference.

rush-hour-anarchic.what: Takes familiar frustration and amplifies it.
rush-hour-anarchic.effect: Helps readers imagine organised chaos becoming pure chaos.

complete-flouting.quote: complete flouting of every type of traffic rule and common sense
complete-flouting.what: Not just breaking rules but abandoning sense itself.
complete-flouting.effect: Shows this transcends normal risk into pure madness.

relished.what: Shows driver's pleasure in the challenge.
relished.effect: Infectious enthusiasm - makes reader understand the appeal.

survival-fittest.effect: Elevates chaos to natural selection - primal competition.

sharp-flick.what: Quick, precise movement in midst of chaos.
sharp-flick.effect: Shows skill required even in mayhem.

no-lane.effect: British humour in face of danger.

nerves-steel.what: Classic description of bravery under pressure.
nerves-steel.effect: Acknowledges genuine danger and courage required.

two-races.effect: Shows complexity - not just donkeys but vehicles racing too.

amazingly-not.effect: Makes donkeys seem professional, dignified amid madness.

dive-ditch.effect: Shows how dangerous the convoy is to bystanders.

yaqoob-loved.effect: Infectious enthusiasm - explains why people do this.

more-colourful.effect: Humour while maintaining propriety about language.

near-pile-up.effect: Everything builds to this moment of near catastrophe.

swerved-tumbled.quote: swerved, lost his footing and he and the cart tumbled over
swerved-tumbled.what: Series of verbs shows how disaster unfolds.
swerved-tumbled.effect: Slow-motion quality to the crash description.

race-over.effect: Sudden stop after all the build-up - anticlimax.

trouble-began.what: Classic storytelling transition to new problem.
trouble-began.effect: Just when you think it's over, new drama emerges.

hundred-punters.quote: over a hundred punters who had all staked money
hundred-punters.what: Reveals gambling aspect of the race.
hundred-punters.effect: Explains why emotions run so high - money at stake.

strong-opinions.what: Understates what are clearly violent disagreements.

voices-raised.quote: Voices were raised, fists were out and tempers rising

nervous-hanging.what: Locals know when situation is genuinely dangerous.
nervous-hanging.effect: Their fear validates the real danger.

volatile-situation.what: Chemical metaphor - could explode any moment.

swallowed-crowd.what: Crowd as monster that consumes people.
swallowed-crowd.effect: Shows how individuals disappear in mob.

getting-nasty.quote: but it's starting to get nasty. I think we should leave
getting-nasty.effect: Creates urgency - need to escape now.

really-enjoyed.what: Yaqoob's pleasure after surviving the chaos.
really-enjoyed.effect: Shows universal appeal of danger survived.

dont-licence.quote: But I don't even have my licence yet because I'm underage!
dont-licence.what: Saves biggest shock for last moment.
dont-licence.effect: Retrospective horror - they survived despite incompetent driver.

hilarious.what: What terrifies Levine amuses the locals.
hilarious.effect: Shows different cultural attitudes to risk.

glad-hadnt.quote: glad he hadn't told me before
glad-hadnt.what: Would have been too scared if she'd known.
glad-hadnt.effect: Sometimes better not to know the danger you're in.

massive-pile-up.effect: Retrospective fear of what could have happened.

high-stakes.what: Juxtaposes serious gambling with humble donkeys.
high-stakes.effect: Captures the absurd seriousness of the event.

entourage.meaning: A group of people attending or surrounding a person
entourage.note: French word meaning the group following someone important. Here used ironically for donkeys.
entourage.effect: Elevates the donkeys to celebrity status, adds humour to the chaotic scene.

overview.heading: Why Levine Wrote This
overview.intro: Levine's purposes evolve through the passage:

points.label: To document unusual sports
points.text: "researching and filming unusual sports" - Shows professional purpose

points.label: To entertain with chaos
points.text: "Formula One without rules" - Makes mundane race exciting

points.label: Western readers seeking adventure
points.text: References to "Wacky Races" and "Formula One" - Familiar comparisons

points.label: Travel enthusiasts
points.text: Exotic location details - Karachi, Pakistan setting

points.label: Humour seekers
points.text: "like maracas" explanation - Makes foreign familiar and funny

points.label: Enthusiastic participant
points.text: "But will you try and get to the front?" - Eager for action

points.label: Self-deprecating humour
points.text: "feeling rather silly" - Laughs at herself waiting

points.label: Exhilarated observer
points.text: "Yaqoob loved it" - Shares in the excitement

points.label: Relieved survivor
points.text: "glad he hadn't told me before" - Retrospective fear

points.label: Racing metaphors
points.text: "Formula One without rules", "neck-and-neck" - Makes chaos comprehensible

points.label: Sensory overload
points.text: "horns tooting, bells ringing" - Cacophony of sound

points.label: Hyperbole
points.text: "waited for eternity", "massive pile-up" - Exaggerates for effect

points.label: Slow build-up
points.text: "waited for eternity" - Creates anticipation through delay

points.label: Explosive middle
points.text: "two races" - Peak chaos with parallel action

points.label: Abrupt ending
points.text: "The race was over" - Short sentence for sudden stop

points.label: Comic revelation
points.text: "don't even have my licence" - Saves best surprise for last
